caveat: Purely mathematical; not attributed to a video source. Checked by script, not by citation.

claim: Softmax uses the same probability mapping as multinomial/conditional logit; the language model as a whole is not a multinomial-logit model.
caveat: Comparison of functional form only; not a claim about model structure, estimation, or interpretability of the network.

claim: For fixed logits, the algebraic odds-ratio property associated with IIA survives; it carries no behavioral random-utility, structural, or welfare interpretation here.
caveat: Algebraic property only. Explicitly not a random-utility or structural claim.

claim: Temperature rescales logits before softmax normalization; as T approaches 0 the distribution converges to argmax when there is a unique highest logit; as T approaches infinity the distribution approaches uniform.
caveat: The tie case for T to 0 is stated on this site; not necessarily discussed at this timestamp in the video.

claim: At each token position the model defines a categorical probability distribution through softmax; training maximizes the conditional likelihood of the observed next tokens across the corpus, equivalently minimizing negative log likelihood (cross-entropy).
source: Andrej Karpathy, "Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT"
caveat: The video demonstrates this via a concrete walkthrough; the maximum-likelihood framing in econometric language is this course's own standard restatement.
